subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw allow selected group/channel peers to share the agent main session, and if so should both global session.groupScope and exact per-binding overrides be public API?
rationale: The request adds compatibility-sensitive config and deliberately collapses an existing conversation isolation boundary; code review alone cannot choose the supported privacy model, peer kinds, or precedence contract.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in
options.body: Accept isolated-by-default groupScope with exact binding precedence after the linked PR proves inbound/outbound routing, upgrade behavior, and privacy warnings.

options.title: Use named shared sessions
options.body: Defer main-specific folding and design one broader canonical session mapping for groups, channels, and threads with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929.

options.title: Retain group isolation
options.body: Reject group-to-main session merging and keep session tools or durable memory as the supported cross-context mechanism.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in
recommendation.body: Accept isolated-by-default groupScope with exact binding precedence after the linked PR proves inbound/outbound routing, upgrade behavior, and privacy warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current routing/config history and already framed the issue’s focused scope and security implications.
